title: Outdoor Things to Do Near Wolfeboro, NH: Hikes, Lakes and Trails
description: Favorite hikes, beaches, paddling, trails and winter fun within about an hour of Wolfeboro, NH, with drive times from downtown and tips on parking.
eyebrow: Wolfeboro, New Hampshire · Within about an hour
h1: Outdoor things to do near Wolfeboro
intro: Wolfeboro sits right where the lakes meet the mountains, so you can swim in the morning and stand on a summit by afternoon. Here are the hikes, beaches and trails locals love, with rough drive times from downtown Wolfeboro.

sections.title: Hikes with a view
sections.lede: Ordered from closest to farthest. Most are fine for kids, and most of them end with a lake view.

items.name: Abenaki Tower
items.stats: About a quarter mile each way · Easy · Free, open year round
items.body: The best payoff for the least effort around here. A short, gently uphill dirt path through the woods gets you to an 80 foot wooden tower, and from the top you look out over Lake Winnipesaukee and the Belknap Range. Kids love the stairs. Grandparents love that it takes ten minutes.
items.tip: The signed lot is on Route 109 between Melvin Village and 19 Mile Bay, across from Wawbeek Road. The top stairs are steep, so hold the rail.

items.name: Copple Crown Mountain
items.stats: 2.8 miles to the summit (about 5.6 round trip) · Moderate · Summit 1,868 ft
items.body: A quiet one. The trail follows old town roads and logging roads through hardwoods, then switchbacks up through spruce for the last half mile. From the top you can pick out Winnipesaukee and Lake Wentworth, plus the Belknaps, the Ossipees and the Sandwich Range.
items.tip: Parking holds only three or four cars at the end of Hanson Road, and the road isn't plowed in winter, so there's no parking then. Go in from Brookfield, not New Durham.

items.name: Mount Major
items.stats: Main Trail 1.5 miles each way · About 1,150 ft of climbing · Moderate · No parking fee
items.body: The Lakes Region classic, and for good reason. The open summit at 1,786 feet gives you the big view straight up Lake Winnipesaukee with the White Mountains behind it. The blue Main Trail is the shortest way up and finishes on steep granite ledges. The yellow Brook Trail is gentler and makes a nice way down, about 3.9 miles for the loop.
items.tip: The lot on Route 11, about 4 miles north of Alton Bay, fills early on summer weekends and foliage days. Go early or on a weekday. The upper ledges are slick when wet or icy.

items.name: Mount Roberts at Castle in the Clouds
items.stats: 2.5 miles each way · About 1,360 ft of climbing · Plan on 3 to 4 hours · Summit 2,582 ft
items.body: A favorite half day with real views. The trail climbs steadily from Shannon Pond, then opens onto granite ledges that look down over Winnipesaukee and the Belknaps, with the southern White Mountains from up top. The same 5,000 plus acre conservation area has around 30 miles of trails, including the Brook Walk past seven waterfalls, the biggest a 40 foot plunge called the Falls of Song.
items.tip: Trails are open year round during daylight hours. Bald Knob, in the same area, is another family favorite with views of Winnipesaukee.

items.name: Red Hill Fire Tower
items.stats: 1.7 miles to the summit · About 1,290 ft of climbing · Moderate · Free
items.body: A wide, well kept trail up to a fire tower with one of the best views in the region: Squam Lake on one side, Winnipesaukee on the other, and the Ossipee, Sandwich and White Mountain ranges all around. You pass the old Horne family homestead on the way. Come back down the Cabin Trail for a loop of about 3.6 miles.
items.tip: Trailhead parking is on Red Hill Road. From the lights in Center Harbor, take Bean Road 1.5 miles, turn right on Sibley Road, then bear left onto Red Hill Road.

items.name: Mount Chocorua by the Piper Trail
items.stats: 4.3 miles each way · About 2,700 ft of climbing · Challenging · Summit 3,500 ft
items.body: If you want a real White Mountains day, Chocorua is within reach. It's a long, steady climb to a bare rocky summit with views in every direction, and the Piper Trail starts right off Route 16 on the south side of the mountains. Pack a lunch and give yourself the whole day.
items.tip: The lot is a large dirt area off Route 16 behind Davies General Store. There are no restrooms or water at the trailhead.

items.name: Belknap Mountain Fire Tower
items.stats: 0.8 to 0.9 miles from the upper Carriage Road lot · About 700 ft of climbing · Summit 2,382 ft
items.body: A fire tower summit in the Belknap Range, and a good one when you want views without a long day. From the upper lot, the green trail is the quick, steeper way up, and the red trail is a little gentler and passes a nice outlook to the west. Do one up and the other down for an easy loop. From the tower you get Winnipesaukee and, on a clear day, Mount Washington.
items.tip: The green trail has ledges that get slippery in the wet, especially coming down.

items.name: West Rattlesnake
items.stats: Old Bridle Path, about 0.9 miles each way · Roughly 400 ft of climbing · Easy
items.body: Short, sweet and right above Squam Lake. It's an easy climb to rocky ledges that look out over the islands. A great one to pair with lunch in Holderness or Center Harbor on the way home.
items.tip: The small lot on Route 113 fills quickly, so get there early.

sections.title: On the water
sections.lede: Winnipesaukee gets the attention, but the smaller lakes around town are just as nice for a swim or a paddle.

items.name: Brewster Beach
items.body: Wolfeboro's town beach on Winnipesaukee, right off Clark Road. It's busy all summer with swim lessons, picnics and kids in the water. In winter the lot is plowed so you can get out on the ice for fishing or skiing.
items.tip: Swim at your own risk when no lifeguard is on duty. Buses aren't allowed.

items.name: Wentworth State Park
items.body: A small, easygoing state park on the shore of Lake Wentworth, the quieter lake just east of town. Good for swimming, picnics and fishing, with picnic tables and flush toilets.
items.tip: In season it's $4 for adults and $2 for kids 6 to 11, and kids 5 and under get in free. Parking is limited on nice weekends, so you can reserve ahead on the NH State Parks site.

items.name: Kayaks and paddleboards
items.body: Wolfeboro Bay is a lovely place to paddle on a calm morning, and Lake Wentworth is a quieter option. Dive Winnipesaukee on North Main Street rents kayaks, canoes and paddleboards by the hour, day or week, with paddles and life jackets included.
items.tip: Call ahead in summer to make sure boats are available: 603 569 8080.

items.name: A cruise on the Mount Washington
items.body: If you'd rather let someone else do the steering, the M/S Mount Washington sails from the Wolfeboro docks in summer, run by a company whose history on the lake goes back to 1872. It's a relaxed way to see the big lake, the islands and the mountains from the water.
items.tip: The Wolfeboro dock is at 11 Dockside Street. Schedules change each season, so check before you go.

sections.title: Walk, bike and wander
sections.lede: Two trail systems you can reach without really getting in the car.

items.name: Cotton Valley Rail Trail
items.body: Twelve miles of hard packed trail on the old railroad bed from downtown Wolfeboro through Brookfield to Sanbornville. It runs along two lakes, over old trestles, past wetlands and fields, and it's mostly easy going with some hills. Walk a mile out and back after breakfast or bike the whole thing.
items.tip: Dogs need to be leashed. Bikes yield to walkers, and everyone yields to the rail cars.

items.name: Sewall Woods
items.body: 179 acres of woods just off Main Street, linked with the town's Abenaki trail network for more than 18 miles of trails. Easy hiking in summer, about 5 miles of beginner to intermediate mountain bike singletrack in spring, summer and fall, and cross country skiing and snowshoeing in winter.
items.tip: Park at the end of Clow Road. Dogs must be leashed. No biking in winter or when the trails are muddy.

sections.title: Winter outside
sections.lede: Wolfeboro doesn't hibernate. When the snow comes, here's where to go.

items.name: Abenaki Ski Area
items.body: Wolfeboro's own little ski hill on Pine Hill Road, with a rope tow, a kiddie tow and some of the most affordable skiing anywhere. It's where a lot of local kids learn, and it's a fun, low key outing for the whole family.
items.tip: For 2026 to 2027 it's set to open December 26, weather permitting. Open Wednesday to Friday 4 to 7 pm and weekends from 11 am. Nonresident day passes are $20 on weekdays and $30 on weekends and holidays. Bring tow gloves.

items.name: Gunstock Mountain Resort
items.body: The big mountain in the Belknaps: 44 trails plus glades, a 1,340 foot vertical, night skiing, tubing and groomed cross country trails. In summer it turns into a mountain coaster and ziplines day.
items.tip: Night skiing runs on 25 trails, so you can fit in a few runs after a day on the lake.

items.name: Cross country skiing at Sewall Woods
items.body: The Wolfeboro Cross Country Ski Association grooms trails right in town, so you can be on skis ten minutes after your coffee. Ungroomed trails are open for snowshoeing.
items.tip: A trail pass is required for the groomed trails. Check the association's website for passes and grooming reports.

items.name: Ice fishing and winter hikes
items.body: When the lakes freeze, the shanties come out. Brewster Beach keeps its lot plowed for winter access to the ice. Mount Major and Mount Roberts are both popular snowshoe hikes, and the Abenaki Tower is lovely in the snow.
items.tip: Only go out on ice you know is safe, and bring microspikes for the ledges on Major.

tips_title: A few tips before you head out
tips: Popular trailheads like Mount Major and West Rattlesnake fill up early on summer and fall weekends. Go early or go on a weekday.
Drive times are rough estimates from downtown Wolfeboro in good conditions. Summer traffic around the lake and snowy roads can add time.
Most of these trails are on conserved land cared for by volunteers. Carry in, carry out, keep dogs leashed where posted, and stay on the trail.
Granite ledges get slick when wet or icy. Bring traction for winter hikes and an extra layer for windy summits.
Hours, fees and schedules change. Check the linked source before you go.
closing: Pair a morning hike with something on the calendar. See what's on in Wolfeboro or browse the Town Guide for food, beaches and rainy day ideas.
